source_name: CERC, RE Tariff Order for FY 2026-27 (Petition 12/SM/2026, 23.08.2026), applying the CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024
source_location: Paragraphs 24-25 'Debt-Equity Ratio', printed page 19 (PDF page 19): Regulation 13(1) of the RE Tariff Regulations 2024 'specifies a debt-equity ratio of 70:30 for the determination of a generic tariff'.
notes: Secondary source. Equity share = 30 percent. The CEA NEP 2022-32 gives no WACC or discount rate (see cea_costs.csv).

source_name: CERC, RE Tariff Order for FY 2026-27 (Petition 12/SM/2026, 23.08.2026), applying the CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024
source_location: Paragraphs 28-30 'Loan Tenure and Interest on Loan', printed pages 21-22 (PDF pages 21-22): Regulation 14(2)(b), normative interest rate = 200 basis points above the average SBI one-year MCLR of the last six months; average MCLR 15.11.2025 to 14.05.2026 = 8.71 percent, so 10.71 percent (paragraph 30).

source_name: CERC, RE Tariff Order for FY 2026-27 (Petition 12/SM/2026, 23.08.2026), applying the CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024
source_location: Paragraphs 26-27 'Return on Equity', printed pages 20-21 (PDF pages 20-21): Regulation 16(2), normative RoE 14 percent (post-tax) for RE other than small hydro, grossed up by the MAT rate of 17.47 percent for the first 20 years: 16.96 percent [14% / (1 - 17.47%)] (paragraph 27).
notes: Secondary source. Pre-tax rate as computed by CERC for the first 20 years of the tariff period; after 20 years CERC grosses up by the corporate tax rate (34.94 percent), giving 21.52 percent, which is not used. Pre-tax WACC = 0.70 x 10.71 + 0.30 x 16.96 = 12.585 percent, our computation.

source_name: CERC, RE Tariff Order for FY 2026-27 (Petition 12/SM/2026, 23.08.2026), applying the CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024
source_location: Paragraphs 9-11 'Discount Factor', printed pages 15-16 (PDF pages 15-16): Regulation 10(2), discount factor = post-tax WACC; 9.08 percent = (10.71% x 0.70) x (1 - 34.94%) + 14.0% x 0.30 (paragraph 11).
notes: Secondary source. Reference only: the CEA-basis cost carries no tax term, so it uses the pre-tax WACC built from the three rows above.

source_name: CEA, Report on Optimal Generation Capacity Mix for 2029-30, Version 2.0 (April 2023)
source_location: Section 8.2.1.2 A 'Cost v/s PLF' and Exhibit 8.6 'PLF vs Variable Cost (Rs/kWh)', printed page 28 (PDF page 34): 'majority of capacity with utilization of more than 60% have variable cost in the range of 1.3 to 3.5 Rs/kWh'; footnote '# All Prices are at 2021-22 Level'.
notes: Secondary source. 2.4 is our midpoint of the printed range 1.3 to 3.5. The variable cost of a coal station is its fuel (energy) charge. Same 2021-22 price level as the NEP capex. Copy hosted by JMK Research (the URL the repository already cites for this report); raw copy in raw/lcoe/cea/.

source_name: CERC, RE Tariff Order for FY 2026-27 (Petition 12/SM/2026, 23.08.2026), applying the CERC RE Tariff Regulations 2024
source_location: Paragraph 50 'Fuel Cost', printed page 28 (PDF page 28): Regulation 38, biomass fuel price for the third year of the control period, 'Other States' Rs 4559.01 per MT; state values range from 4193.01 (Tamil Nadu) to 5074.84 (Punjab).
notes: Secondary source. FY2026-27 price level (CERC escalates the FY2024-25 notified price by 3.45 percent a year), not the 2021-22 level of the NEP capex. Fuel cost = heat rate (4200 kcal/kWh, cea_costs.csv; also CERC paragraph 44) / GCV x price, our computation: 4200 / 3100 x 4.55901 = 6.177 Rs/kWh.
